raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
torch.compile on zimage-base gets 1.42x faster: steady-state denoise at
1024x1024 goes 13.575 s -> 9.577 s on one H100, from a single kernel.

Z-Image reuses one transformer block for the context refiner (a few dozen
caption tokens), the noise refiner (4096) and the unified stream (4128 at
1024x1024). The flash-attn call breaks the graph, so the block's attention
compiles into a frame of its own that is entered with all three counts;
automatic dynamic shapes make its token dim symbolic, and Inductor autotunes the
fused-qkv GEMM once, against whichever count it traced first. The caption branch
wins that race and the resulting BLOCK_M=32/BLOCK_N=32 config then runs the
4096- and 4128-token layers too. It is the only dynamic-shape Triton template
the model selects, and it accounts for the entire difference above. The same
gap appears in the comparison table in BBuf/how-to-optim-algorithm-in-cuda#21.

Set inductor's multi_kernel_hints for this model, so the block is compiled once
per hint and dispatched on the runtime shape and the token dim stays dynamic.
The knob is a generic DiTConfig.torch_compile_inductor_config passthrough that
is empty for every other model; inductor config is process-global and is read
when a graph compiles, so it cannot be scoped to the torch.compile call, and
`mode` rules out torch.compile(options=...).

The root cause is the flash-attn graph break, which is what routes three very
different token counts through one compiled frame. Removing it would help any
DiT with mixed sequence lengths and is worth doing separately.

Test Plan:

Steady-state denoise on one H100, min of requests 2..8 (request 1 carries the
compile), stock preset with no extra flags:

```
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CI=1 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \
       FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1
B=python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile/scripts/bench_diffusion_denoise.py
rm -rf ~/.cache/sgl_diffusion/torch_compile_cache
python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label compile --output-dir /tmp/zb
python3 $B --model zimage-base --iterations 8 --label eager --no-torch-compile --output-dir /tmp/zb
```

| arm                  | denoise  |              |
|----------------------|----------|--------------|
| torch.compile before | 13.575 s |              |
| torch.compile after  |  9.577 s | 1.42x faster |
| eager, for reference |  9.567 s |              |

First-request e2e goes 79.6 s -> 96.2 s, the cost of autotuning the block at two
sizes instead of one. Verified from the generated code that the fused-qkv site
is now autotuned at 32, 64, 4096 and 4128 rather than at 32 alone.

nodes.body: Can we use this optimization to other models?

> Can we use this optimization to other models?

What's happening is that the dimension is marked as dynamic and Inductor autotunes it on the first shape it sees, which happens to be far off the common case. This passes the shape hint to Inductor. Most of the changes in this PR are to pipe through the config and that, we can very well use for other models too!

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) data point: this does not improve the current main stack on this GPU, so I think the hint should be architecture/version-gated unless a current H100 recheck still shows the original gap.

I rebased head `75971562c4bb` onto current main `bede6bc37c5d9638099ebb948d93b9e2a7799f10` and ran the registered `zimage-base` preset with the official `Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image` snapshot at `04cc4abb7c5069926f75c9bfde9ef43d49423021`, 1024x1024, 50 steps, seed 42.

Environment: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96 GiB), driver 595.84, CUDA 13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130` (`cf30153c4c13`), Triton 3.7.1.

| arm | denoise | step 0 | median steps 2..49 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main eager, mean of 2 runs | 16.361 s | - | - |
| main compile, cold cache | 17.729 s | 1268.4 ms | 327.45 ms |
| this PR, cold cache | 18.218 s | 1736.1 ms | 327.93 ms |
| this PR, second process reusing the same cache | 18.526 s | 1779.4 ms | 327.05 ms |

The steady-state steps are effectively tied; the PR is 2.76% slower than current-main compile on the measured request and 11.35% slower than eager. The second-process full-model cache reuse completed successfully, but did not recover performance.

Most importantly, current-main Inductor already autotuned the real large shapes separately on this stack. The baseline log contains `AUTOTUNE mm(4096x3840, 3840x11520)` and `AUTOTUNE mm(4128x3840, 3840x11520)`, selecting cuBLAS at about 0.90 ms. I therefore did not see the caption-sized `BLOCK_M=32` kernel being reused for the 4096/4128-token QKV GEMM on SM120.

Outputs were deterministic within each compiled arm (both PR runs had the same PNG SHA-256). Relative to eager, main compile was SSIM 0.88433 / PSNR 24.41 dB and the PR was SSIM 0.88361 / PSNR 24.33 dB, so there was no compensating quality benefit.

Rechecked on H100 against current main (`024a7a1031`). Rebased this branch onto it, pushed as `a0fa3d1a7c`. Same preset and snapshot as you (`Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image` @ `04cc4abb7c50`, 1024x1024, 50 steps, seed 42). TP=1, one H100 96GB @650W. 8 requests, first discarded, cache purged before each compile arm.

| arm | denoise, median req 2..8 | median step 2..49 |
|---|---:|---:|
| main eager | 9.482 s | 188.00 ms |
| main compile | 13.322 s | 264.54 ms |
| this PR | **9.438 s** | **187.93 ms** |

1.41x over main compile. Eager parity. So the gap is still open on H100.

The autotune log says why. Main specialises `mm(4096x3840, 3840x11520)`, like you saw. But there is no entry for 4128. That is the unified stream, most of the work. It falls back to the kernel picked for the caption branch. With the hint we get 32, 64, 4096 and 4128. Your log has 4128 already, so on SM120 there is nothing to fix.

Two notes. Your 2.76% is the measured request, which pays for the extra autotuning — your own steady-state steps were tied, 327.93 vs 327.45 ms. Same here: first-request e2e 78.9 -> 97.5 s, steady state unchanged. And gating on arch is a proxy; the real trigger is whether Inductor specialises 4128. Root cause is the flash-attn graph break. I'd fix that separately. Happy to gate on SM90 for now if you prefer.
@BBuf , can you also take a look at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36399 which solves the warmup issue?

@@ -46,6 +46,10 @@ class DiTConfig(ModelConfig):

     torch_compile_mode: str = "max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"
 
+    # torch._inductor.config overrides for this model, applied before compiling,
+    # e.g. {"multi_kernel_hints": [64, 4096]}.
+    torch_compile_inductor_config: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
     @staticmethod
     def add_cli_args(parser: Any, prefix: str = "dit-config") -> Any:
         """Add CLI arguments for DiTConfig fields"""

@@ -2,7 +2,7 @@
 
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
-from typing import Tuple
+from typing import Any, Tuple
 
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.dits.base import DiTArchConfig, DiTConfig
 
@@ -96,3 +96,10 @@ class ZImageDitConfig(DiTConfig):
     arch_config: ZImageArchConfig = field(default_factory=ZImageArchConfig)
 
     prefix: str = "zimage"
+
+    # One block serves both the caption tokens (tens) and the image and unified
+    # streams (thousands), with a dynamic token dim, so its GEMMs get autotuned
+    # for one branch and run for all three -- 1.4x slower when that goes wrong.
+    torch_compile_inductor_config: dict[str, Any] = field(
+        default_factory=lambda: {"multi_kernel_hints": [64, 4096]}
+    )

 )

             config=dit_config,

+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
 
 def maybe_enable_inductor_compute_comm_overlap() -> None:
@@ -19,6 +22,17 @@ def maybe_enable_inductor_compute_comm_overlap() -> None:
         pass
 
 
+def apply_inductor_config(overrides: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Apply a model's torch._inductor.config overrides before it is compiled."""
+    import torch._inductor.config as _inductor_cfg
+
+    for name, value in overrides.items():
+        if not hasattr(_inductor_cfg, name):
+            logger.warning("Unknown torch._inductor.config option %r, ignoring", name)
+            continue
+        setattr(_inductor_cfg, name, value)
